title: Ordered sum-affine chart adjunction and counit under model changes
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ and let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with $NR=0$. Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, put $V=\mathbf A^d_Y$ for an integer $d\geq0$, and let $e:U\to V$ be separated etale of finite type, with $U$ Noetherian and $g=p_de$. Choose compactifications of $e,p_d,g$ with Noetherian middle schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], compact-support candidates $F_{e,R},F_{d,R},F_{g,R}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], exact sum extension $E_R=De_{\Sigma!,R}$ and exact inverse image $e_R^*$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Specify a graph-normalized comparison datum [def-sp-etale-compact-support-normalization], with $c_{e,R}:F_{e,R}\simeq E_R$, and canonical composition $\alpha_R:F_{d,R}F_{e,R}\simeq F_{g,R}$ [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Put $\lambda_R=\alpha_R F_{d,R}(c_{e,R}^{-1})$.
Use the ordered affine-space adjunction $F_{d,R}\dashv G_{d,R}$, $G_{d,R}=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$, of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported to the chosen compactification by its canonical comparison; here $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ and $(d)$ is tensor with its $d$th tensor power. In dimension zero this is the identity adjunction. Give $E_R\dashv e_R^*$ its degreewise sum/evaluation adjunction [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison], with counit $v_R$, and write $\epsilon_{d,R}$ for the actual ordered affine counit and $H_R=e_R^*G_{d,R}$.
On bounded-below inputs the Hom bijection of the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], precomposed by $a\mapsto a\lambda_{R,M}$, defines the specified chart adjunction $F_{g,R}\dashv H_R$. Its actual counit is
$$\epsilon_{g,R,K}=\epsilon_{d,R,K}\circ F_{d,R}(v_{R,G_{d,R}K})\circ\lambda_{R,H_RK}^{-1}.$$
For second compactification models, denote the common-refinement comparisons by $\rho_{d,R},\rho_{g,R}$ and form the primed adjunctions by the same ordered construction. Then
$$\epsilon'_{g,R,K}\circ\rho_{g,R,H_RK}=\epsilon_{g,R,K},$$
and the corresponding composite counits $\delta_R=\epsilon_{d,R}F_{d,R}(v_RG_{d,R})$ satisfy $\delta'_R\circ(\rho_{d,R}E_R)H_R=\delta_R$. Changing the model of $e$ leaves this sum adjunction unchanged. The identifications satisfy the common-refinement cocycle laws and retain the actual sum-then-affine counit for every model.

source.place: Charts, sum-then-ordered-affine counit; old scalar-normalization Step 2 and the counit part of Step 5

proof.text: Suppress $R$. Let $P$ be the ordered affine left functor before choosing the model of $p_d$, and let $\kappa:P\simeq F_d$ be its canonical comparison. The affine node supplies $P\dashv G_d$ with its specified counit, and its transport along $\kappa$ is the adjunction in the statement. The sum adjunction is the degreewise adjunction of [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison], with counit $v$. Apply the composite-adjunction formula to $E\dashv e^*$ followed by $F_d\dashv G_d$. Its right functor is $H=e^*G_d$, its Hom equivalence is the two specified Hom equivalences in that order, and its counit is $\delta_K=\epsilon_{d,K}\circ F_d(v_{G_dK})$. All compact-support identifications here and below are used on bounded-below inputs, as in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. The functors $E$ and $e^*$ are exact, $F_d$ is a candidate $Rr_*Dj_!$, and $G_d$ is inverse image, tensor with the locally free rank-one Tate power and shift; all four preserve bounded-below objects, so both adjunctions and their composite restrict to the full bounded-below subcategories with the same Hom bijections and counits. Lean implementation: boundedness on every D+ input uses the natural affineTraceRight_normalForm, flatness of the finite Tate line, the Tor-amplitude tensor lower-bound lemma and exact inverse image. The Hom and counit formulas are the component formulas of Mathlib Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft and Adjunction.comp.

source.place: Charts, sum-then-ordered-affine counit; old scalar-normalization Step 2 and the counit part of Step 5

proof.text: The isomorphism $\lambda=\alpha\circ F_d(c_e^{-1})$ has source $F_dE$ and target $F_g$. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso] to the composite adjunction of Step 1 and $\lambda$. This gives exactly the prescribed Hom map $a\mapsto\Phi(a\circ\lambda_M)$, where $\Phi$ is the composite Hom equivalence. To calculate its actual counit, take $M=HK$: the inverse image of $1_{HK}$ under $\Phi$ is $\delta_K$, so under the new equivalence it is $\delta_K\circ\lambda_{HK}^{-1}$. This is the displayed formula for $\epsilon_{g,K}$, including the specified sum/evaluation and ordered affine counits.

source.place: Charts, sum-then-ordered-affine counit; old scalar-normalization Step 2 and the counit part of Step 5

proof.text:
Write $\rho_e:F_e\simeq F'_e$ as well as $\rho_d,\rho_g$. Refinement compatibility in the supplied graph-normalized datum gives $c'_e\rho_e=c_e$; the same identity for a common-refinement comparison follows by composition and inversion. Hence $(c'_e)^{-1}=\rho_ec_e^{-1}$. Independence of choices for the canonical composition in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] gives
$$\alpha'\circ F'_d(\rho_e)\circ(\rho_dF_e)=\rho_g\circ\alpha.$$
Naturality of $\rho_d$ at $c_e^{-1}:E\to F_e$ now gives, by substitution,
$$\lambda'\circ(\rho_dE)=\alpha' F'_d(\rho_e)F'_d(c_e^{-1})(\rho_dE)=\rho_g\alpha F_d(c_e^{-1})=\rho_g\lambda.$$
Thus changing only the model of $e$ leaves $\lambda$ itself unchanged under the fixed comparisons for $p_d$ and $g$. Lean implementation: the unbounded common-refinement cocycle and every-tower compositor equation identify each actual model composition with the same chosen-model compositor. Refinement normalization of M first gives comparison_change; cancellation gives comparison_inverse_change. Substitution and naturality give chart_to_chosen and then chart_change. These identities hold on all inputs, and are specialized to the bounded-below inputs in the conclusion.

source.place: Charts, sum-then-ordered-affine counit; old scalar-normalization Step 2 and the counit part of Step 5

proof.text:
Let $\kappa':P\simeq F'_d$. Coherence gives $\kappa'=\rho_d\kappa$. The same inverse-Hom calculation as in Step 2 gives $\epsilon_{d,K}=\epsilon_{P,K}\kappa_{G_dK}^{-1}$ and $\epsilon'_{d,K}=\epsilon_{P,K}(\kappa'_{G_dK})^{-1}$; therefore $\epsilon'_{d,K}\rho_{d,G_dK}=\epsilon_{d,K}$. Naturality of $\rho_d$ at $v_{G_dK}:Ee^*G_dK\to G_dK$ gives
$$\delta'_K\rho_{d,EHK}=\epsilon'_{d,K}F'_d(v_{G_dK})\rho_{d,EHK}=\epsilon'_{d,K}\rho_{d,G_dK}F_d(v_{G_dK})=\delta_K.$$
This is the claimed identity for composite counits; no replacement of a counit by an unspecified adjunction is involved. The ordered affineComparison changes only in its final model comparison: at zero apply the common-refinement cocycle, and at a successor apply composition_change_target to the fixed preceding stage. No induction hypothesis on the preceding stage is required. Cancel its hom component to obtain the counit transport equation, and use naturality to obtain the composite counit equation.

source.place: Charts, sum-then-ordered-affine counit; old scalar-normalization Step 2 and the counit part of Step 5

proof.text:
Evaluate Step 3 at $HK$ and invert its isomorphisms to obtain $(\lambda'_{HK})^{-1}\rho_{g,HK}=\rho_{d,EHK}\lambda_{HK}^{-1}$. Steps 2 and 4 then give
$$\epsilon'_{g,K}\rho_{g,HK}=\delta'_K(\lambda'_{HK})^{-1}\rho_{g,HK}=\delta'_K\rho_{d,EHK}\lambda_{HK}^{-1}=\delta_K\lambda_{HK}^{-1}=\epsilon_{g,K}.$$
For three models, the comparison identities and cocycle laws of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] imply $\kappa''=\rho'_d\rho_d\kappa$ and $\lambda''(\rho'_d\rho_d)E=(\rho'_g\rho_g)\lambda$; substituting in the same formulas proves the asserted coherence for the actual adjunctions and counits. The sum adjunction uses only $e$, so is unaffected by its compactification. For $d=0$, take $P=1$ and $\epsilon_P=1$: all formulas reduce to the sum counit with the canonical identity-model comparison.
